newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DALY SHOOTS RECORD-TYING 66 TO LEAD PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DALY SHOOTS RECORD-TYING 66 TO LEAD PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: John Daly, who quit in the middle of the last major championship he played, shot a record-tying four-under-par 66 on Thursday to take the early lead in the PGA Championship -- the tournament that launched his mercurial career in 1991.

Daly, a recovering alcoholic who walked off the course after 27 holes in the U.S. Open in June because he still had the shakes due to a drinking binge in March, posted an impressive seven birdies on Winged Foot Golf Club's vaunted West Course while making only three bogeys.
"I hit a lot of fairways and made some putts," Daly said after matching the competitive course record that his friend Fuzzy Zoeller set in winning the 1984 U.S. Open here.
Daly's lead was being threatened, however, by Davis Love, who was four under par after eight holes. Love eagled the 515-yard fifth hole to jump into contention.

The 31-year-old Daly, who won the 1995 British Open in a playoff, said Wednesday's sporadic rains had softened the greens and made them more receptive to approach shots on Winged Foot's long dogleg par-4s.

"The greens were perfect this morning," said the newly slimmed-down Daly, who did not have a birdie putt longer than 15 feet. "They were softer than yesterday, which made it easier to throw the ball right at the flag."

As Jack Nicklaus predicted before the tournament, experience, especially in major championships, paid off at Winged Foot, which he said was one of the toughest courses in the world, especially when set up for a major championship.

Veteran Tom Kite, the 47-year-old U.S. Ryder Cup captain, and two former PGA Championship winners, Paul Azinger and Bob Tway -- along with young British Open champion Justin Leonard -- were closest to Daly among those in the clubhouse.
They all shot two-under 68 on a warm, sunny day.

Leonard, 25, won the day's unofficial match among the winners of the year's first three majors as he outscored Masters champion Tiger Woods and U.S. Open winner Ernie Els. They all played together in the "dream" threesome of the first two rounds.

Woods, 21, and South African Els, 27, both matched par 70 after adventurous rounds in which each made a double bogey -- Els at the 442-yard eighth and Woods at the 540-yard 12th. They were in a big group at 70.
Phil Mickelson, another under-30 star, 1993 U.S. Open winner Lee Janzen, and relative unknowns Doug Martin and Tom Byrum were at one-under 69 as Winged Foot remained resistant to sub-par scoring.

After getting off to a fast start with three consecutive birdies on the front nine, Woods, playing in his first PGA Championship, gave those strokes back in two holes coming home -- the double at 12 and a bogey at 14.

Els, who won his second U.S. Open at Congressional Country Club, also struggled after a good start. He was three under after seven holes but then went five over in the next seven before he righted himself with birdies at 16 and 18.
While the slightly soft conditions made Winged Foot's notoriously-hard greens a little more receptive, not everyone found the famous course easy.
Britons Nick Faldo and Darren Clarke, joint runner-up to Leonard in the British Open at Troon last month, both struggled. Faldo shot 75 and Clarke 74.
Jesper Parnevik of Sweden, runner-up at Troon for the second time at a British Open, shot 76, as did two-time U.S. Open champion Curtis Strange.
Former Masters champions Ben Crenshaw and Ian Woosnam of Britain both shot 77s.
